heading: Clock and secure random numbers
body:
Tachyon gives every Tac service two small browser APIs: `Clock` and `SecureRandom`. Tachyon writes them once in the page, and each language reaches them through a small client.

| Language | How the service gets them | Clock | SecureRandom | A failure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JavaScript, TypeScript | `@Needs clock` and `@Needs secureRandom` | `now()`, `monotonic()`, `timeZone()` | `bytes(count)`, `uuid()` | an error is thrown |
| Rust | fields `clock: Clock` and `secure_random: SecureRandom`, which `Default` fills | `now_ms()`, `monotonic_ms()`, `time_zone()` | `bytes(count)`, `uuid()` | an `Err` value |
| Go | `// @Needs` above `clock Clock` and `secureRandom SecureRandom` | `NowMs()`, `MonotonicMs()`, `TimeZone()` | `Bytes(count)`, `UUID()` | an `error` value |
| C# | `private readonly Clock clock = new();` | `NowMs()`, `MonotonicMs()`, `TimeZone()` | `Bytes(count)`, `Uuid()` | an `InvalidOperationException` |
| F# | `let clock = Clock()` and `let secureRandom = SecureRandom()` in the type | `NowMs()`, `MonotonicMs()`, `TimeZone()` | `Bytes(count)`, `Uuid()` | an `InvalidOperationException` |
| Kotlin | `private val clock = Clock()` and `private val secureRandom = SecureRandom()` | `nowMs()`, `monotonicMs()`, `timeZone()` | `bytes(count)`, `uuid()` | an `IllegalStateException` |
| Java | `private final Clock clock = new Clock();` and `private final SecureRandom secureRandom = new SecureRandom();` | `nowMs()`, `monotonicMs()`, `timeZone()` | `bytes(count)`, which gives a `byte[]`, `uuid()` | an `IllegalStateException` |
| Swift | `private let clock = Clock()` and `private let secureRandom = SecureRandom()` | `nowMs()`, `monotonicMs()`, `timeZone()` | `bytes(count)`, `uuid()` | an error is thrown; call with `try` |
| Dart | `@Needs()` above `final Clock clock;` | `nowMs()`, `monotonicMs()`, `timeZone()` | `bytes(count)`, `uuid()` | a `StateError` |
| Ruby | `Clock.new` and `SecureRandom.new` | `now_ms`, `monotonic_ms`, `time_zone` | `bytes(count)`, `uuid` | a `RuntimeError` |

`now` is the time in milliseconds since 1970 (UTC). `monotonic` only goes up, so it measures how long something takes. `timeZone` is the time zone of the browser, such as `Europe/Paris`. `bytes` gives 0 to 65,536 random bytes from `crypto.getRandomValues`, and `uuid` gives a random version 4 UUID.

The page answers at once, so no call waits. These two APIs need no permission, so the manifest grants nothing for them. A service that is linked into a native app has no page, so the build refuses these APIs in it (`TY1317`). A test unit has no page either: give the calls fake answers (see "Browser APIs in test units"). The fields are not shown to the view.
